title: Your team is 100% certified. Is anyone actually using the new messaging?
summary: Hyperbound Initiatives, included in Hyperbound Perform, tracks messaging behavior on every real sales call and delivers rep-level feedback and practice for each missed moment.
body_markdown:
You launch new messaging the way everyone does. A kickoff session, a messaging guide, a certification roleplay. Within two weeks the completion number reads 100%. Leadership sees the slide, the program is delivered, everyone moves on.


Then a month later someone asks the obvious question, in a meeting you would rather not be in: are reps actually using it with customers?


Nobody knows. Sales calls get recorded, but no one on the team has time to listen to hundreds of them looking for a specific phrase. The reps who are not using it have already built their own workaround, and it is working well enough that they are not going to volunteer it. By the time the quarterly business review surfaces the problem, the rollout is a quarter old and the reps who missed it have missed it for three months of pipeline.


Quick takeaways


- Completion rates measure training, not behavior. Report consistency on real calls instead.
- Check a rollout while it is live, not at the end of the quarter.
- Pair every missed moment with feedback right away, while the call is still fresh.


## Why completion is the wrong number


Certification answers a real question, and it is worth being fair to it: can this rep deliver the message once, under observation, with the material in front of them? That is not nothing. It is a floor.


It is also not the question enablement is being asked. A rep can pass a certification on Friday and run their old pitch on Monday, because Monday is a live call with a real buyer and an unscripted objection, which is a different task entirely. Completion measures who finished. It does not measure who changed.


Most enablement leaders know this, which is why the completion number tends to be reported with a slight apology attached. The problem is that the alternative, listening to calls, has never been practical. As[a review of what managers actually see in call recordings](https://www.hyperbound.ai/blog/what-sales-managers-can-see-from-call-recordings) makes clear, frontline managers listen to less than 1% of the calls their team records. That is not a discipline problem. It is a bandwidth problem: one manager, five to ten reps, and a stack of recordings that grows faster than any single person can review. When the alternative is manually reviewing a fraction of the evidence, completion wins by default.


## The real problem is three separate problems


**Calls are recorded, but nobody has time to listen.** The evidence exists. The attention does not. No amount of prioritization fixes that, because call volume grows faster than anyone's calendar.


**Feedback arrives late or never.** When a manager does find a call where a rep missed something, the feedback reaches the rep days later, detached from the moment. By then the specific thing that went wrong has blurred into general feedback.


**Building practice for every new talk track takes time nobody has.** The obvious fix, practice, has its own cost: someone on the enablement team has to write a roleplay for each new message, then keep writing them as the message evolves. That is a project per rollout, and the third one never gets built.


## What enablement actually needs


Three requirements, and it is worth reading them against the products you already own before anyone shows you a feature list.


**See whether the behavior is happening on real calls, while the rollout is live.** Not a report at the end. A running view during the months when you could still do something about it.


**Act on the gaps right away, for the reps who need it.** Finding the problem is half a system. The other half is that the rep who missed something hears about it while the call is still fresh, and gets practice on that specific moment rather than a reminder to review the messaging guide. Enablement that arrives detached from the moment tends to be treated like any other doc that lives outside the workflow: ignored.


**Do it without adding work for enablement.** If the fix requires your team to write roleplays and run reviews, it becomes another program to staff, and it will be the first thing cut in a busy quarter.


## Introducing Hyperbound Initiatives


[Hyperbound](https://www.hyperbound.ai/) is an AI sales coaching platform that helps sales teams practice and improve their conversations. Hyperbound Initiatives is a system for autonomous behavior change, included in[Hyperbound Perform](https://www.hyperbound.ai/product/hyperbound-perform) , the part of Hyperbound that scores and analyzes your team's real sales calls.


Initiatives picks up where certification stops. Enablement leaders describe the behaviors they want to see on real calls, and Initiatives checks every eligible call for them for as long as the rollout runs. When a rep misses one, they get feedback on that exact moment plus a short practice session built for their next similar conversation. Consistency is visible on the dashboard while the rollout is still live.


Here is the loop, in four steps.


**1. Set it up by describing it.** You tell Kota, Hyperbound's AI assistant, where you set things up by describing what you want, the behaviors you need and which calls they apply to. Alternatively, upload the messaging guide or battle card and let Kota pull the behaviors out. If you are not yet sure what to look for, ask Kota to review recent calls and surface the biggest gaps first, then turn those into an initiative. Each initiative takes up to three behaviors, in priority order.


**2. Test it before anyone sees it.** A test run on past calls shows which calls would have counted, whether each behavior happened, and exactly what each rep would receive. Nothing is sent to anyone until you publish. That is the step that matters most to teams who do not want a new system emailing their reps on day one.


**3. It checks every eligible call.** Calls are filtered by type, situation, competitor, or words on the call, so a rep is not measured on conversations where the behavior never applied. When a rep misses a behavior, they get written feedback on the moment, plus a bite-sized roleplay on that one behavior. They see it on their Hyperbound homepage and by Slack or email. Initiatives works with calls recorded in Hyperbound or imported from other recorders, including Gong and Chorus.


**4. You see the results.** The dashboard shows who is consistent, by week, team, and behavior, down to the exact moment on a call where something was missed. Past calls play back from the dashboard, so a gap identified for a specific rep arrives with the evidence attached.


## What changes for enablement


Four things, and they map directly to the four things that were broken.


**See it.** Enablement leaders can answer "is this landing?" during the rollout instead of at the quarterly review. Consistency is measured over a rolling window of recent calls, so a rep who improves shows up as improving.


**Act on it.** Every missed moment becomes feedback and a practice session, built by the system rather than by the enablement team. Each practice session uses the rep's real stakeholder and company context, so almost no two reps receive the same exercise.


**Stay in control.** Enablement decides which calls count, which reps are included, and when the initiative runs. The start date can be backdated by up to a month to see where the team stood before the rollout, and individual reps can be exempted.


**No extra lift.**[Initiatives is part of Hyperbound Perform](https://www.hyperbound.ai/product/hyperbound-perform/initiatives) at no extra cost, and nobody on the enablement team is writing roleplays.


Try this (45 minutes, no tools needed)


Audit your last rollout in three steps.


1. Pick its single most important behavior, and write it as a “Did the rep …?” question.
2. Sample 10 recent calls per rep and mark whether the behavior happened. Your recordings already have this; you are just counting.
3. Compare how many reps did it on most of their calls with your completion rate.


The gap between those two numbers is your case for change, and it is usually bigger than people expect. Doing it for one team takes an afternoon. Doing it for five teams, every week, is why we built this.


## For Hyperbound customers


Start with one initiative and a small pilot group, not the whole team. Pick a rollout that is live right now, test it on past calls first, and look at what your reps would actually receive before you publish. The test run is where you refine the criteria. Talk to your account manager about setup, and about which of your current rollouts would be the best first one.


Where this fits alongside what you already have: Hyperbound Practice, the part of Hyperbound where reps rehearse sales conversations with realistic AI buyers, is where onboarding and one-time certification belong. Initiatives is for the months after, when reps are on real calls and you need to know whether the rollout held.
